la:verb:edo.html:
ē-do, dĭdi, dĭtum, 3, v. a.,
to give out, put forth, bring forth (freq. and class.).
In gen.: foras per os est editus aër,; cf.: sputa per fauces tussi,: urinam,; cf. stercus,: animam, to breathe out, i. e. to die, expire, ; 9, 62; cf.: extremum vitae spiritum,: vitam,; : clamorem,to send forth, utter,; cf.: miros risus,: fremitum patulis sub naribus (equus),: voces,: dulces modos,: questus,: hinnitus,: latratus, et saep.: Maeander in sinum maris editur,discharges itself,; fin.: clanculum ex aedibus me edidi foras,have slipped out,.
In partic., to bring forth any thing new, to produce, beget, form, etc.
Of what is born, begotten (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): progeniem in oras luminis,: crocodilos dicunt, cum in terra partum ediderint, obruere ova, deinde discedere,; so, partum,; cf.: aliquem partu,; ; : aliquem maturis nisibus,: geminos Latona,: nepotem Atlantis (Pleïas),: (draconem) Qui luci ediderat genitor Saturnius, idem Abdidit, Cic. Poëta Div. 2, 30, 64; cf.: Electram maximus Atlas Edidit,.—In the pass.: hebetes eduntur,. —More freq. in the part.: in lucem editus, Poëta ap. (a transl. of the Euripid. τὸν φύντα); cf. : editus partu,; 9, 678; : Venus aquis,; cf.: Limnate flumine Gange,; for which: de flumine, (cf. Zumpt, Gramm. § 451): ille hac,; cf.: Maecenas atavis regibus,: infans ex nepte Julia, et saep.—
Transf.: (tellus) Edidit innumeras species,; cf. : frondem ulmus,puts forth,: ea (sc. academia) praestantissimos in eloquentia viros edidit,.—
Of literary productions, to put forth, to publish (class.): de republica libros,; so, librum contra suum doctorem,: annales suos,: orationem scriptam,: aliquid,; ; ; ; et saep.—
Transf., to set forth, publish, relate, tell, utter, announce, declare = exponere; esp. of the responses of priests and oracles, the decrees of authorities, etc.: apud eosdem (sc. censores) qui magistratu abierint edant et exponant, quid in magistratu gesserint,; cf. : ede illa, quae coeperas, et Bruto et mihi,: nomen parentum,; ; : veros ortus,; cf.: auctor necis editus,: mea fata tibi, et saep. —With acc. and inf.: Apollo Pythius oraculum edidit, Spartam nulla re alia esse perituram, etc.,; cf. ; ; .—With dupl. acc.: auctorem doctrinae ejus falso Pythagoran edunt,; cf. ; fin.: haec mihi, quae canerem Titio, deus edidit ore,: iis editis imperiis,; cf.: edito alio tempore ac loco (with constitutum tempus et locus),: opinio in vulgus edita,spread abroad,; cf. : consilia hostium,i. e. to divulge, betray, et saep.—Poet.: arma violentaque bella,i. e. to sing, celebrate in song,.—Hence,
Jurid. and polit. t. t., to give out, promulgate, proclaim, ordain: qua quisque actione agere volet, eam prius edere debet. Nam aequissimum videtur, eum, qui acturus est, edere actionem, etc., (tit. De edendo), 1 sq.: verba,; cf. judicium,: tribus, said of the plaintiff in a causa sodaliciorum, to name the tribus (since he had the right, in order to choose the judges, to propose to the defendant four tribus, from which the latter could reject only one, and then to choose the judges according to his own pleasure out of the remaining three, sqq.: judices editi (= editicii),; cf. Wund. p. LXXVI. sq., and see editicius: socium tibi in hujus bonis edidisti Quintium,hast mentioned,: quantum Apronius edidisset deberi, tantum ex edicto dandum erat,; : mandata edita, ; cf. : ederet (consul) quid fieri velit,to command,; cf. .—
Transf. beyond the jurid. sphere: postquam hanc rationem cordi ventrique edidi, etc.,.—
Of other objects, to produce, perform, bring about, cause (freq. and class.): oves nullum fructum edere ex se sine cultu hominum et curatione possent,: vitales motus,: proelia pugnasque,; ; ; ; cf. caedem,; : strages, and 527: aliquantum trepidationis,; cf. tumultum,: ruinas,: scelus, facinus,to perpetrate,: annuam operam,i. e. to perform,; cf. ; : munus gladiatorium (with parare),to exhibit,; ; cf. ludos,; ; : spectaculum,; ; et saep.: gladiatores, et saep.: exemplum severitatis,; so more freq.: exempla in aliquem,; ; and 27; cf.: scelus in aliquem,.
To raise up, lift, elevate: corpus celerem super equum,.—Hence,
ēdĭtus, a, um, P. a. (set forth, heightened; hence, like excelsus).
Prop., of places, elevated, high, lofty (cf.: altus, celsus, excelsus, sublimis, procerus, arduus, praeceps, profundus), opp. to flat, level (cf.: collis paululum ex planitie editus,; ; ; —very freq. and class.): Henna est loco perexcelso atque edito,; (with acclivis); 7, 18, 3; ; ; ; et saep.—Comp., ; ; . —Sup., Auct. B. Alex. 28; 31; 72; —*
Trop.: viribus editior,stronger,.—Adv. does not occur.—
ēdĭtum, i, n.
A height: in edito,: ex edito,.—Plur.: edita montium,; : in editis, Treb. Trig. Tyr. 26.—
Transf., a command, order, ; cf. .

la:noun:edictum.gloss: a proclamation, ordinance, edict, decree or manifesto by a magistrate
senses: a proclamation, ordinance, edict, decree or manifesto by a magistrate
the public announcement of the praetor or other senior magistrate, in which he states, on entering upon his office, the rules by which he will be guided in administering justice; inaugural address
la:noun:edictum.html:
ēdictum, i, n.
id.
.
A proclamation, ordinance, edict, manifesto of the Roman magistrates (cf.: senatus consultum, scitum, jussum; decretum, epistola, rescriptum), e. g. of the ediles,; ; ; ; of a tribune of the people,; of a dictator,; of the consuls,; ; of the proconsuls,; of Caesar in the civil war,; of the emperor,; (cf. decretum, epistola, rescriptum) et saep.—
Esp. freq. the public announcement of the praetor, in which he states, on entering upon his office, the rules by which he will be guided in administering justice (out of such legal regulations renewed and made more complete every year—edictum perpetuum, in contradistinction to edicta prout res incidit; cf. —there was gradually formed an important part of the body of Roman law), ; ; sq.; ; et saep.; cf. Sanders, introd. p. xviii. sq.; xxiv. sq.; ; Rein's Privatr. p. 70 sq.; 80; 83, and the sources cited.—
Transf., in gen.
An order, command, .—
A play-bill, order of games: edictum et ladorum ordinem perlegere,: his mane edictum, Gildersleeve ad loc.

senses: to make known (of a decree), proclaim; enact a law
la:verb:edico.html:
ē-dīco, xi, ctum, 3 (old form,
subj.: EXDEICATIS; gerund.: EXDEICENDUM, S. C. de Bacchan.; imperat.: edice,; ), v. a.
A t. t. of magistrates, to declare, publish, make known a decree, ordinance, etc.; hence, to establish, decree, ordain by proclamation (cf.: praecipio, mando, jubeo).
In gen., with ut or ne: consulem edicere, ut senatus senatusconsulto ne obtemperet ... edicere est ausus, ut senatus ad vestitum rediret,; so ; ; cf. in the abl. part. perf.: edicto, ut and ne,; ; ; and with a simple subj.: cum tribuni plebis edixissent, senatus adesset, etc.,; so ; .—With acc.: non proscriptā neque edictā die,; so, dies edicta,: diem comitiis,; fin.: diem exercitui ad conveniendum,; cf. ; : justitium,: comitia a. d. XI. Kal. Febr.,: senatum in diem posterum,; cf. : conventum sociis Tarraconem,: novemdiale sacrum,; cf.: supplicationem populo in diem unum,: delectum,: praedam omnem militibus, et saep.—With an obj. acc. and inf.: edixit, sese judicium injuriarum non daturum,; so ; .— Absol.: quod Vitellius de caerimoniis publicis edixisset,; cf.: de natali suo,: de iisdem,. —
In partic., of the praetor, to make known, on entering upon his office, the principles on which he intends to administer it: est tibi edicendum quae sis observaturus in jure dicendo,; v. edictum.
Transf. in gen., to make known, dectare, appoint, establish, order, ordain any thing (freq. and class.): ut tu scire possis, edico tibi: Si falsa dices, etc.,; cf. ; .—With ut or ne, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; —With acc. and inf.: dico, edico vobis, nostrum esse illum erilem filium,; nullus fere ab eo (sc. Demosthene) locus sine quadam conformatione sententiae edicitur,— With rel. clause: jussus a consule, quae sciret edicere,to discover, communicate, give notice, Kritz.: si prius, quid maxime reprehendere Scipio solitus sit, edixero,: hoc simul edixi,; : incipiens stabulis edico in mollibus herbam Carpere oves,; cf. ; ; : legem remittere edixit (rex),.—
To explain, interpret (late Lat.): sensum hujus sermonis,; .

la:verb:educo.html:
ēdŭco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
1. educo, II. A. 4. b.
,
to bring up a child physically or mentally, to rear, to educate (very freq. and class.): educit obstetrix, educat nutrix, instituit paedagogus, docet magister, Varr. ap. (but this distinction is not strictly observed; see the foll. and 1. educo, II. A. 4. b.).
Prop.: hera educavit (puellam) magna industria,: Athenis natus altusque educatusque Atticis,: bene pudiceque educatu'st usque ad adolescentiam, et saep.; cf. ; ; Att. ap. ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; . —
Transf., to bring up, rear, foster, train, educate: neque enim hac nos patria lege genuit aut educavit, ut, etc.,; ; cf.: ars dicendi ea, quae sunt orta jam in nobis et procreata, educat atque confirmat,: in his (scholis) educatur orator,: oratorem, id. prooem. § 5: illos in disciplina,.—
Poet. and in post-Aug. prose, of plants or animals, to nourish, support, produce: quod pontus, quod terra, quod educat aër Poscit,; cf. : vitis mitem uvam,: pomum, non uvas (ager),: herbas (humus),: Caecuba,: florem (imber),: lepores, apros,.—
To possess, hold (cf. nutrire = τρέφειν), .

la:verb:edissero.html:
ē-dissĕro, rŭi, rtum, 3, v. a.,
to analyze in words, to set forth, unfold, explain, relate, tell (rare but class.): jam animum advorte ac mihi quae dicam edissere,; cf.: neque necesse est edisseri a nobis quae finis funestae familiae,; and: cum agi, non quemadmodum agantur, edisseri oportet,: Laelius eadem edisseruit (for which, shortly before, exposuit),: res gestas,: cunctandi utilitates,: viam gerendi belli,: haec vera roganti, * : tantum hoc, * : somnium,to interpret,: parabolam,.—Absol.: quis (Catone) in docendo edisserendoque subtilior?.—With rel. clause, .

la:verb:edoceo.gloss: to teach, instruct or inform thoroughly
senses: to teach, instruct or inform thoroughly
la:verb:edoceo.html:
ē-dŏcĕo, cŭi, ctum, 2, v. a.,
to teach thoroughly; to instruct, inform, apprise one of any thing (class.; for syn. cf.: doceo, perdoceo, erudio, praecipio, instituo). —With acc. pers. and rei: eadem haec intus edocebo, quae ego scio, Stratippoclem,; so ; ; ; ; cf. in the pass.: Cicero per legatos cuncta edoctus,; ; ; ; and with acc. pers. and inf.: Etruscam Edocuit gentem casus aperire futuros,; cf. in the pass.: edoctus tandem deos esse,.— With acc. pers. and rel. clause: quos ille edocuerat, quae dici vellet,; so ; cf. in the pass.: ante edocti, quae interrogati pronuntiarent,; : eadem fere quae Volturcius de paratis incendiis senatum edocet (Kritz. docet),: ab Evandro edocti,; cf.: tot cladibus edocti,; and: in qua (disciplina) edoctus esset,: aliquid,: omnia ordine,.— With interrog. clause: quid fieri velit, edocet,; ; ; cf. ; and with obj. acc. and inf., : ut edoceas, ut res se habet,.—With acc. pers. and subj. clause: Phanium edocebo, Ne quid vereatur Phormionem,.—
Transf., of abstract subjects: fama Punici belli satis edocuerat, viam tantum Alpes esse,: edocuit tamen ratio ... ut videremus, etc., * .—Hence, * ēdŏcenter, adv., instructively: scriptum est,.

Prop.: (Roma) edomito sustulit orbe caput,; cf. .—
Transf.: pastinaca edomita, opp. agrestis,: aes igni,to melt,: ramum oleae curvando,: vitiosam naturam ab eo sic edomitam et compressam esse doctrina, ut, etc., * (al. domitam): feritatem,; : nefas, * : labores,: lumina,to lull to sleep,.
